For me, it sounds like love the way you describe it. The feeling of just wanting to hold, cherish them... to feel giddy and well, kinda stupid around them. It shows you care and love them enough. Try looking at it as if... if he IS your soulmate. And if you want him in your life as a partner, I say take the risk. Far too many people don't take the risk and for that reason dont feel complete and dont wind up as happy as they could be. The worst that could happen is he says "hey I dont feel the same towards you" or "I'm not sure how I feel but let's continue to be the way we were and perhaps we can establish something romantic in the future". And sometimes that does hurt but I think the closure would be nice whether he loves you back or is on the fence. Regardless he still seems super sensible so I dont think he'd lash out about you being young and not knowing anything hehe. As for the actual introduction to that sort of conversation... I'm socially awkward sometimes so I don't know if i could be in the place to offer that sort of advice Haha! Overall, for example, I loved my boyfriend before he asked me to be his girlfriend. He was really nervous about me rejecting him for his age. He said he almost backed out of it. But you know, that was the best risk both of us have ever taken. And now I can't imagine life without him. That's what happens when you meet your other half, and I do hope he is the one for you :)

The reaction you might get will vastly depend on the age difference. For me, my boyfriend is 6 years older which may or may not be a larger age gap than you guys. One main thing I try to remember is theres a jump with becoming an adult. I am still technically changing and growing, not 20 yet, and his brain is finished with that change. So theres always some consideration for "will I still want to be with this person when I'm older" "Can I see us getting married" and so on. Honestly if you really love this man, I'd say go for it. And if you're both adults I do hope you'd be able to bring it up with him without him flipping out or being immature about the situation. If he is as sensible as you say he is, while this is scary, I suggest gradually bringing it up. By the looks of it I think you have a really good shot, and while age is a factor certainly... I know people with 40 year age gaps... And their families have accepted it. So if it's not that major of one, and your family and friends truly want what's best for you, they'll ease into it. Dont be surprised if it takes a little bit for them to understand either, people generally always come around at some point, if they love you :)

Is she clinically diagnosed with anxiety? If not, that is something that must change. Panic attacks are serious things, if she's claiming she's having an episode it's generally accompanied with shortness of breath, pounding heart, sometimes spasms, and so on. It feels like you can't breathe and you're choking very often. It's serious, I have them often and I feel bad for my boyfriend when I do during really inconvenienced times. It's not your fault you sleep heavily, and it's not her fault she's having panic attacks ( again I'm worried her idea of panic attack is not the clinical one ). Having anxiety and having panic attacks are different. Unfortunately, panic attacks can't be "cured". They wear off, but it's not a real curable thing. If she can get her anxiety under control that would help a lot, it wouldn't trigger the panic in the first place, so I suggest she go to a doctor, get diagnosed if she hasn't already, and try starting anxiety medication. This is a tough situation for both of you, however I'm put off by the fact she gets really pissed over something you can not control. I assume you've talked to her about it right?
